articles.headline: Stop Counting Hours. Your Sleep Schedule Matters More Than You Think
articles.body: You've heard eight hours is the magic number. New research is flipping that advice. Sleep regularity—keeping consistent bedtimes and wake times—is a stronger predictor of health outcomes than total sleep duration, including mortality and cardiometabolic disease risk. This means that a stable sleep schedule, even if slightly shorter, may protect you better than chasing nine hours on an irregular pattern. Your body's internal clock values consistency over volume.
articles.takeaway: Prioritize going to bed and waking at the same time daily. This rhythm matters more than hitting a perfect hour target.

product.name: LectroFan White Noise Machine
product.blurb: Blocks ambient noise so your sleep is actually restorative.

articles.headline: The Mineral Your Stressed Brain Needs But Probably Lacks
articles.body: Magnesium doesn't just quiet muscle tension—it silences the stress response itself. Studies show supplementation lowers cortisol, the stress hormone that worsens anxiety when chronically elevated. The effect is dose-dependent and measurable within weeks. People with low magnesium levels see the biggest gains. Your nervous system runs on this mineral, yet most adults are deficient. When you're under sustained pressure, your magnesium depletes faster, creating a downward spiral. Restoration works.
articles.takeaway: If stress is constant and your sleep is inconsistent, magnesium glycinate 300-400mg daily may reset your nervous system faster than willpower alone.

product.name: Pure Encapsulations Magnesium Glycinate
product.blurb: The most underused sleep and recovery tool. Most athletes are deficient.

articles.headline: Scientists Found a Hidden Gut Bacterium That Separates Healthy People From Sick Ones
articles.body: A previously unknown group of gut bacteria called CAG-170 appears far more often in healthy individuals and much less frequently in people with chronic disease. Researchers at the University of Cambridge analyzed over 11,000 human gut samples from 39 countries and found these microbes are stable over time. They support other beneficial bacteria while producing vitamin B12—essentially playing a structural role in a healthy gut ecosystem. This discovery reframes the microbiome conversation: it's not just about what you add, it's about maintaining the bacteria that hold the whole system together.
articles.takeaway: Rather than chasing probiotics, focus on fiber-rich foods and fermented options that feed the diverse bacteria already working for you.

articles.headline: The Molecule Your Cells Use to Repair Damage Declines With Age. Here's Why Scientists Are Watching
articles.body: NAD+ is your cell's energy regulator and repair supervisor. It powers ATP production, fixes DNA damage, and maintains mitochondrial function. But NAD+ levels naturally decline as you age, and this depletion correlates directly with memory loss, muscle weakness, and higher disease risk. Recent expert reviews in Nature Aging bring together evidence that restoring NAD+ through vitamin B3 precursors or targeted interventions shows promise. The research is advancing rapidly, though long-term human safety data is still accumulating. This isn't a miracle molecule—it's a foundational one.
articles.takeaway: NAD+ boosters remain experimental for most people. Focus on proven basics first: exercise increases NAD+, as does good sleep and caloric restriction.

workout.title: Press & Burn: Dumbbell Push Circuit
workout.warmup: Start with 90 seconds of arm circles, forward and back. Follow with 10 slow shoulder rolls, 10 scapular push-ups, and a 30-second chest opener in a doorframe. Get your joints warm before you load them.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Floor Press
exercises.notes: Lie flat, lower slowly to a 2-count, press strong. Keep ribs down and core tight throughout. Modify: use lighter dumbbells or reduce to 3 sets.

exercises.name: Standing Dumbbell Overhead Press
exercises.notes: Press straight up, don't arch your lower back. Lock out fully at the top, control the descent. Squeeze glutes to keep your core braced.

exercises.name: Push-Up Negative (3-Second Lower)
exercises.notes: Lower yourself in 3 slow seconds, then push back up at normal speed. This is where the real strength is built. Drop to knees if needed to keep form clean.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
exercises.notes: Lead with your elbows, not your wrists. Stop at shoulder height. Use lighter weight than you think you need. No swinging.

exercises.name: Tricep Dumbbell Kickback
exercises.notes: Hinge forward at the hip, elbow locked at your side, extend fully. Squeeze at the top for one second. The lockout is the money rep.

workout.cooldown: Finish with a 60-second chest stretch in a doorframe each side, then a 60-second overhead tricep stretch per arm. Shake out your hands and roll your shoulders back a few times.
workout.description: Warmup: Start with 90 seconds of arm circles, forward and back. Follow with 10 slow shoulder rolls, 10 scapular push-ups, and a 30-second chest opener in a doorframe. meal.title: Chicken & White Rice Bowl with Steamed Carrots
meal.description: A bland, easy-to-digest pre-race meal designed to fuel without shocking your gut. The soft carbs and lean protein give you glycogen without fiber or fat that slow digestion.
meal.instructions:
1. Boil or steam carrots until tender, about 8 minutes.
2. Pan-sear chicken breast in olive oil over medium-high heat for 6–7 minutes per side until internal temp reaches 165°F.
3. Slice chicken and arrange over warm white rice.
4. Add steamed carrots to the side.
5. Season lightly with salt and pepper; eat 2–3 hours before race start.
meal.tip: White rice and carrots are low-FODMAP and low-fiber, making them ideal for race morning. Cook rice the night before and reheat, or use microwaveable rice packs for zero stress.
